subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled session-memory filenames and `# Session` headers use `agents.defaults.userTimezone` instead of host/TZ local time when those differ?
rationale: Current shipped docs and code define session-memory as host-local, but auto-flush memory already follows the configured user timezone; changing filenames is user-visible and compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Adopt existing userTimezone
options.body: Align session-memory with auto-flush by using `agents.defaults.userTimezone` for filenames, fallback HHMM slugs, and headers without adding config.

options.title: Keep host-local session-memory
options.body: Preserve the shipped host-local contract and close or narrow this request to docs explaining the distinction.

options.title: Add a dedicated memory timezone
options.body: Introduce a separate memory artifact timezone setting only if maintainers want memory behavior decoupled from prompt/envelope user timezone.

recommendation.title: Adopt existing userTimezone
recommendation.body: Align session-memory with auto-flush by using `agents.defaults.userTimezone` for filenames, fallback HHMM slugs, and headers without adding config.

likelyOwner.reason: This person merged the current host-local session-memory behavior and is the clearest routing candidate for deciding whether to change that shipped artifact contract.
